profile.headline: Software Developer for the UNL Police Department
profile.summary:
As a computer science instructor, I knew my students needed a solid foundation through theory and reenforced with practical application (primarily programming assignments). There was no assignment I gave to my students that I did not complete myself first. This enabled me to better understand the difficulties they may have completing the assignment. I pushed my students beyond their comfort level so they would be prepared for a career as an IT professional and/or graduate school. If students had trouble understanding a concept I would be willing to change my approach within the lecture or give individuals one-on-one time. I was also willing to do whatever it took to help a student learn the material as long as they were willing to give an appropriate effort.

As a software developer, I consider myself a "logical problem solver" who utilizes my computer science and mathematics background to create computer software. I have found changing programming languages (20 languages in the past 30 years) is relatively simple (that's just language syntax), but the most difficult part is learning a new application domain or new programming paradigm. I have been exposed to many different programming paradigms (and programming languages):
	• Procedural – Ada, C, FORTRAN & Pascal
	• Declarative – LaTex, lex/yacc, Prolog & SQL
	• Functional – APL & LISP
	• Object-Oriented – C++, Delphi & Java
	• Event-Driven – Javascript & Visual Basic

Specialties: Computers: Alpha, Cyber, Harris, PC, PDP-11, Sun & VAX 
OS: UNIX (Ultrix, Solaris & Linux), VMS & Windows (MS-DOS)
DBMS: dBase, Access, MS-SQL & MySQL
Languages: Ada, APL, Assembly, C/C++, Clipper, CLIPS, COBOL, FORTRAN, Java, Javascript, LISP/Scheme, Pascal, Perl, PHP, PL/1, Prolog, RPG, Snobol & VB6/VB.net
Paradigms: Procedural, Declarative, Functional, Object-Oriented & Event-Driven
Other Tools: AJAX, bash, Crystal-Reports, CSS, HTML, JSON, LaTex, lex/yacc, OpenGL, sendmail, SQL, SVG, TCPDF, VBA, & vi

company.name: Shared Computing Services at the University of Nebraska - Lincoln

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description: I'm currently converting legacy software, from Windows-based to web-based, used by the Police Department's Record-Management-System (RMS) at UNL and UNO. A single instance of the RMS system includes 8 applications (6 web-based apps and 2 console-based apps), 170+ database tables and 800+ stored-procedures. The ultimate goal is to eventually migrate this software for UNK's Police Department. Data is stored within a SQL-Server database, and other software development tools being utilized are: .NET Framework, T-SQL, Crystal-Reports, HTML5, CSS3, SVG, XML, Javascript, JQuery & AJAX.

positions.title: Database Developer and Analyst
positions.description: I design and implement software used by the CYFS community in the assimilation of “high quality interdisciplinary research to promote the intellectual, behavioral, and social-emotional development and functioning of individuals across educational, familial, and community contexts.” Data is retrieved via VB.net and PHP applications and then exported to SPSS for analysis. I utilize the following software tools: VB.net, PHP (Dreamweaver), HTML5, Excel-Reader, TCPDF, Javascript (AJAX & JSON), CSS, SVG, SQL, MySQL (Navicat) & SPSS.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description: I designed and implemented proprietary software used for client profiling, investment research, portfolio management, and performance measurement, and integrated it with an off-the-shelf portfolio management system (TechFi, PowerAdvisor & PortfolioCenter) utilizing the following software tools: Visual Basic, VBA, SQL, ADO, MS Access, & MS SQL Server (Toad). One software project that I created from beginning to end is called "Style Analysis". It performs statistical analysis utilizing multiple regression on more than 6,500 mutual funds to determine the investment style of an individual fund from 20 years of monthly performance. The resulting statistics are given to the investment team and used to help them determine whether a fund should be placed on the hire list. I also, developed the company’s web-site utilizing the following software tools: HTML, Perl, PHP, Javascript, CSS, SVG, FPDF, XML, sendmail, SQL & MySQL (Navicat).

positions.title: Computer Science Instructor
positions.description: I taught 9 sections of computer science and advised 20 students per year. During my entire tenure I taught 24 different courses of which 15 were upper-level (including: Data Structures, Organization of Programming Languages, Operating Systems, Database Systems, Computer Graphics, Numerical Analysis, Object Oriented Programming, and Software Engineering). On a part-time basis, I lectured 40 hours of seminars on programming languages, reviewed 21 manuscripts (including a 500 page Ada textbook for DC Heath), and implemented 8 software projects.

positions.title: Associate Instructor of Computer Science
positions.description: I taught 4 sections of Introduction to Computers and Programming, while on sabbatical from McMurry.

positions.title: Computer Science Instructor
positions.description: I taught 3 computer science courses and a mathematics course.

positions.title: Computer Programmer
positions.description: I wrote dBase III programs for billing, payroll, and membership validation.
